subject: Outcomes signoff & validation plan for BrightWell pilot
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Carey Hall <carey.hall@brightwellhealth.com>, procurement@brightwellhealth.com
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-06-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Outcomes signoff & validation plan for BrightWell pilot

Hi Carey / BrightWell procurement team,

Thanks again for the time yesterday — really excited to move towards a short, measurable evaluation that proves production economics and safety for your claims-processing use case. Attached is a compact mutual action plan (MAP) that maps tasks, owners, and acceptance tests. High-level ask: please confirm that these success tests and the proposed 4-week timeline match BrightWell's expectations so we can lock resources and a reserved evaluation window.

Summary (one line): 4-week pilot to validate integration, latency & throughput, accuracy on a 1k sample benchmark, and operational observability needed for an initial cutover. If BrightWell hits the exit gates below we’ll proceed to a limited-production canary.

Key acceptance tests (short):
- Integration smoke: API calls from your staging to Redwood with sample payloads (pass = <5% error responses, auth + schema validated).
- Latency SLO: p95 generation latency <= 450ms for typical 512-token session during our reserved slot.
- Accuracy / concordance: >88% concordance with your human-reviewed labels on a 1,000-record sample (we provide scoring harness).
- Cost profile: Estimated cost per 1k queries within 15% of the baseline we shared in the estimate.
- Safety / red-teaming: No high-severity policy violations on our test set; automated filters engaged.

Proposed timeline (high level):
Week 0 (kickoff): integration credentials + MAP signoff
Week 1: integration + smoke tests
Week 2: baseline runs + sampling + performance profiling
Week 3: edge-case QA + cost tuning (batching/quantization suggestions)
Week 4: final acceptance run and signoff decision

Deliverables we will provide:
- Scoring harness and sample prompts (Git repo + instructions)
- SOC2 summary and security evidence (attached)
- Redwoods' MAP spreadsheet with owners and dates (attached)

Please reply with any changes to acceptance thresholds, or flag any internal reviewers (security / legal / procurement) to add to the thread. If you confirm this week schedule I’ll lock the Redwood reserved slot for 6/9–7/6 and calendar invites for the kickoff.

Thanks,
Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0124

From: Carey Hall <carey.hall@brightwellhealth.com>

Date: 2025-06-01T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Outcomes signoff & validation plan for BrightWell pilot

Thanks, Karthik — this is a helpful, compact plan. A couple of clarifications from our side before we sign: 

1) Concordance: our clinical ops team typically requires >=90% on high-sensitivity labels. Is 88% a flexible suggestion? We can provide a stratified 1k sample focused on higher-risk categories.
2) Latency SLO: our integration will be in us-west; do you have a separate p95 target for bursty vs steady traffic? We need to understand tail behavior under load.
3) Security evidence: procurement will need SOC2 Type II report highlights (not the full report) plus an explanation of data retention and key management.
4) Acceptance signoff: who signs for BrightWell? Our PM (Asha Patel) will own functional acceptance; procurement wants a short procurement checklist.

We’ll attach our procurement checklist and proposed PO template — can Redwood confirm the SLA window and the estimated monthly spend for the pilot so we can route to finance?

If you can address the above I’ll route to legal / procurement and we should be able to greenlight kickoff next week.

Best,
Carey
Carey Hall
Head of Product Ops, BrightWell Health
carey.hall@brightwellhealth.com

On Sun, Jun 1, 2025 at 11:03 AM Carey Hall <carey.hall@brightwellhealth.com> wrote:
> Thanks, Karthik — this is a helpful, compact plan. A couple of clarifications from our side before we sign: 
> 
> 1) Concordance: our clinical ops team typically requires >=90% on high-sensitivity labels. Is 88% a flexible suggestion? We can provide a stratified 1k sample focused on higher-risk categories.
> 2) Latency SLO: our integration will be in us-west; do you have a separate p95 target for bursty vs steady traffic? We need to understand tail behavior under load.
> 3) Security evidence: procurement will need SOC2 Type II report highlights (not the full report) plus an explanation of data retention and key management.
> 4) Acceptance signoff: who signs for BrightWell? Our PM (Asha Patel) will own functional acceptance; procurement wants a short procurement checklist.

Thanks for the quick read — answers inline below and a firm timeline proposal.

1) Concordance: we can target 90% concordance on your stratified high-risk sample (we’ll run an initial baseline and iterate). We typically set the public-facing threshold a little lower to be conservative during tuning, but for BrightWell high-sensitivity slices we’ll set 90% pass.

2) Latency: for us-west reserved capacity we expect steady-state p95 <= 450ms; under a short, bounded burst (up to 2x nominal concurrency) p95 may rise to ~600ms — we’ll instrument and report p50/p90/p95/p99 for each run. We’ll include load characterization in the week-2 performance report.

3) Security evidence: attached is a SOC2 summary (controls & scope) and a short KMS/HSM note. We’ll also provide a readout that maps BrightWell data flows to our retention policy and encryption model. If you need the full Type II we can start the process but timelines differ.

4) Acceptance signoff: noted — Asha Patel as functional owner is fine. For procurement signoff we typically need a PO from finance + a short acceptance email from the functional owner after the final acceptance run. I’ll add a one-page procurement checklist to the MAP.

Proposed refined acceptance tests (concrete):
- Integration smoke: 200 API calls from staging with schema validation (pass = auth + <3% schema errors).
- Concordance: 90% on BrightWell high-risk 1k sample (scoring harness will be run by Redwood, results shared in Drive).
- Latency: p95 <= 450ms steady, p95 <= 600ms during bounded burst.
- Error budget: <0.5% 5xx responses during test windows.
- Observability: token-level cost and per-route latency breakdown available in Console and exported as CSV.

Timeline (firm): kickoff 2025-06-09; final acceptance run 2025-07-04; decision and signoff by 2025-07-06.

We’ve provisionally reserved the us-west slot and can share calendar invites once you confirm procurement/PO route.

Drive links: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcdEFgHIjKLmnoPqRS/view (scoring harness + sample prompts)

Attaching: soc2_summary.pdf and updated MAP spreadsheet.

Thanks,
Karthik

Carey / team — thanks for the quick cadence here. Karthik: appreciate the clarified thresholds. I approve locking the MAP and the 6/9 kickoff from Redwood's side. A couple internal notes (FYI for BrightWell):

- If the acceptance run is met, we will enable a limited production canary for a narrow tenant slice and monitor for 2 weeks before a broader cutover.
- For any SLA exceptions that require credits we’ll handle via the procurement checklist (Jonas to be the escalation lead for any exceptions during pilot).
- Monica will drive the integration checklist and be your engineering point-of-contact during week 1.

Carey — please confirm Asha Patel as the functional sign-off contact and route PO/contract redlines back to procurement@brightwellhealth.com; we’ll prioritize the kickoff calendar once we see the PO path.
